questions.answer: When a price changes, the trigger records the old and new values in price_audit.
questions.explanation:
When a price changes, the trigger records the old and new values in price_audit.
Why: A VIEW is a named SELECT query, not a separate copy of the data. A trigger runs automatically after an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE and can enforce rules such as writing an audit record. Stored procedures and functions keep program logic in the database; PostgreSQL and MySQL support them with different languages and syntax. SQLite supports triggers but does not provide a server-style stored procedure system. Assign ownership of each rule clearly instead of duplicating it in both the application and a trigger.
